errors: No mathematical errors; the page contains only definitions and methodological remarks. The unit relations (2 Fuß = 1 Elle; Ruthe = 10 or 12 Fuß, depending on decimal or duodecimal measure) are standard period conventions, though the Elle varied regionally.

results.what: Classification of the parts of a mathematical exposition: definitions, theorems, corollaria, postulata, solutio with proof, scholia, lemmata, hypotheses
results.usually_credited_to: Christian Wolff (Anfangs-Gründe aller mathematischen Wissenschaften, 1710), after Euclid and Proclus

results.what: Definition of magnitude as that which can be increased or decreased; homogeneity as measurability by a common unit
results.modern_name: Classical definition of quantity (Größe) and commensurable measure

deep.surprise_reason: A printed page from a standard 18th-century German elementary textbook with routine Wolffian methodological definitions. It is not in Gauss's hand and has no original mathematical content. The only handwriting visible is the edge of the facing leaf, a list of Euler's publications.

checkable.asserts: In the next page's example, AB measured by the common unit F contains 14 units (DC=2F, DE=3F, EB=4F, AC=5F); this sum is my inference, not stated on the page.
In duodecimal measure 12 Zoll = 1 Fuß (Zoll = 1/12 Fuß), as stated across pp. 3-4.

transcription_corrections: First word is most likely 'seyn müßte' (period spelling, cf. 'seyn' later on the page) rather than 'sein müßte'; the image partly obscures it.

The '[Margin, cut off at left edge:]' fragments are not marginalia of this page. They are the visible right-hand edge of the facing handwritten leaf (the previous page's Euler bibliography) and should be attributed to that page, not to folio 3.
The page is printed (Fraktur typeset, signature 'A 2'), not a manuscript; the transcription should note this.
